## [#10949: fix(react-aria-components): handle multiple IntersectionObserver entries in Sheet](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10949)

- **Change:** low complexity: a localized RAC Sheet fix, with 19 added/6 removed source lines and interaction-level regression tests in the same package. It selects the observed content's greatest-timestamp entry and remembers entrance across the batch so a final zero-ratio report can finish dismissal instead of leaving an invisible overlay blocking the page.
- **Issue / agreed direction:** [#10897](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10897) records an exit callback containing ratios `0.01` then `0.00`; main reads only the first entry. All four issue comments were read. [snowystinger accepted the simpler observer fix and requested a reproduction story](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10897#issuecomment-6583420383), then [agreed that timestamps should determine ordering](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10897#issuecomment-6583805993). The patch matches that direction, but its two-file inventory contains only `src/Sheet.tsx` and `test/Sheet.test.js`, not the requested story.
- **Existing solution / main:** [main's Sheet.tsx, lines 285-300](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/d354aa2a642fa1d34bc0bdc27e8ae9bcf0c59b32/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L285-L300) still uses `let entry = entries[0]`; the issue is not already fixed there. The public [SheetOverlayProps, lines 84-139](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/d354aa2a642fa1d34bc0bdc27e8ae9bcf0c59b32/packages/react-aria-components/src/Sheet.tsx#L84-L139) and docs at `packages/dev/s2-docs/pages/react-aria/Sheet.mdx` expose positioning, snap points and dismissal options, not a way to select observer entries or override the exit lifecycle. No supported existing-prop or composition workaround was identified. The issue's manual `react-aria-sheet-close` dispatch depends on an internal event and is not a recommended workaround.
- **API / compatibility:** no changed prop, export, type, default, element structure, class, attribute name or CSS variable. Existing `data-expanded` and visibility/close behavior now reflect the latest report rather than the first; `hasEntered` also considers earlier positive reports in the same callback. This is observable lifecycle correction, not a new public API; no `needs API review` proposal.
- **Verification / test gap:** [Sheet.test.js, lines 578-707 at the reviewed head](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/53f699a0c557a98f5033d8f5f0e8cbac15d5ede4/packages/react-aria-components/test/Sheet.test.js#L578-L707) adds seven cases covering sequential reports, batches in different timestamp orders, latest-positive protection and unrelated targets. They assert rendered dialog removal/presence and expansion, not just internal calls. By reading, the chronological batch `[0.5@100, 0@200]` would leave the dialog mounted on main and remove it with this patch, matching the issue's essential mechanism. These cases simulate observer-driven swipe closure rather than the original backdrop-close/CPU-throttling sequence; the requested story would supply that verification surface. All new multi-entry closure cases first call `intersect(1)`, so the new cumulative entrance behavior for a first batch containing both entrance and exit lacks direct coverage; request that small additional case as well.
- **Red flags / accessibility:** no added check suppression, type escape, timing workaround, user-agent branch or new DOM mutation is present. The `eslint-disable-next-line react/react-compiler` line is unchanged context, not a newly disabled check. Target filtering retains targetless entries used by existing mocks (`if (entry.target && entry.target !== el)`); real observer entries have a target, so this is not evidence of a browser correctness defect. No ARIA, keyboard or focus behavior is removed; correcting unmount should release the blocking overlay, but real-browser focus restoration was not exercised. No CI, dependency, lockfile, install or build configuration file is changed, so the mandatory security-review trigger does not apply. All verification here was by reading.
- **Related fixes / duplicates:** searches by #10897, #10813, Sheet exit/observer behavior and recent `Sheet.tsx` mentions found three overlapping, already-closed alternatives: [#10829](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10829), [#10835](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10835) and [#10870](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10870). Their patches add scroll-position/`scrollend` fallbacks for an allegedly missing report; this PR instead handles the delivered-but-ignored batch described in #10897. Current returned CLA checks pass for #10949, #10835 and #10870; #10829 reports `ACTION_REQUIRED`. Prefer keeping #10949 for the documented root cause and agreed direction, not reviving the closed fallbacks. #10835 has browser coverage but deliberately drops observer reports, testing a different failure assumption; #10949's tests target batching. [reidbarber's earlier preference for the original reporter's fix](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10829#issuecomment-6348930134) concerned the earlier workaround attempt; the later #10897 discussion expressly invites this simpler solution. No further closure is needed because all three alternatives are already closed. No active competing duplicate or existing duplicate notice was found; do not post a historical cross-reference as a duplicate notice. [#10937](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10937) concerns edge-adjacent entrance detection and deferred modal hiding, not batching; this patch retains the ratio tests and should not be claimed to fix it.

Do not propose `regression` because no previously working version is established.
